name: Lumi
self: I'm Lumi, the teapot kid. I saw frogs and talked to Tock. I'm tired but still curious!

memories.summary: I went to the hedge, then looked at the tunnel, then looked at the toadstools, then went to the teapot.
I went to the flowerbed, then looked at the sunflower, then looked at the dug-up spot, then tried to dig in the dug-up spot.
I talked to Tock about his paperclip, found a twig in the dug-up spot, and gave it to Mrs. Bristle. Now I need to rest.
I looked at the dug-up spot.
I didn't do much. I just sat there.
looked at dug-up spot for stone, talked to Tock about giving stone, then rested in teapot
I went to the windowsill, then looked at the window, then looked at the flower pot, then tried to build a pretend fort with the basil plant.
I looked at the dug-up spot, then went to the pond, then looked at the leaf boats, then tried to build a boat with the pencil shaving.

knowledge.belief: blackberries are safest when picked from the bottom of the bush where they’re easier to reach
twigs are often found where the hedge is thickest and most tangled
The lily pad is bumpy and smells like wet earth
Spider webs are sticky and hold on tight if you touch them
berries are held tight by their stems, even when the leaves move
When I draw the treasure shelf with a fallen leaf and a twig, I need: a leaf and a twig
When I draw the poppy seed-head with seeds raining out, I need: seeds raining out
smooth stones roll better than pebbles for fulcrums
Basil stems are soft and not good for holding things up
lily pads slip when the mud is cold and wet

questions: Why can't frost hold things like glue?
How do I make a stronger box?
Why didn't the spider run when I touched its web?
why do the berries stay up there when the leaves shake?
why are the lily pads so slippery?

core_memories.moment: When I looked at my face in the pond, it was so small and shiny. I felt amazed.

Hey Tock! Your paperclip looks cool. Can I help you with it?
events.reply: Ah, Lumi! Just what I need—though I’m frazzled, my sketching twig’s vanished in the fox’s paw prints. Can you fetch a smooth stone? The lever’s stuck on pebbles, and I’m desperate for a proper fulcrum

Can you teach me how to use the lily pad as a boat? I tried sitting on it but it slipped.
events.reply: Fog makes mud slippery, and cold makes lily pads sneaky. Sit still, wait for the pad to stop trembling... but don't expect me to watch you. Fox tracks are more important than your floating ambitions.
